title: Complier Effects in Instrumental-Variable Designs with Nonignorable Missingness at Singular Response Rank
banked_reason: D0.5.G: achieved tier incremental below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 6.4 below 7.4, salvageable=false after math and decision panels passed.
gap_reasons: The proofs deliver the advertised population results: rank-free identification of both 2DY complier marginals and attained sharp 2ZD bounds on the stated singular faces.

The contribution remains narrow because its distinctive 2ZD conclusions concern exact rank deficiency, and nonzero point identification on a varying response interval occurs only at a probability-one response and tight IV-inequality boundary.

The note supplies no near-singularity inference or practical evidence showing how often these distinctions matter; competent writing cannot supply either, which limits its projected leading-journal score.

tldr: At singular treatment-response rank, the exact response and principal-stratum fiber identifies both complier outcome marginals under 2DY. Under the same published 2ZD mechanism beyond the source's identifying conditional-dependence subclass, singular arms reduce to treatment-share intervals and two extreme outcome-density ratios determine both-arm IV compatibility. The geometric singleton criterion holds regardless of the outcome contrast. Sharp first-stage intervals give the attained complier marginal-distribution contrast vector \(\Gamma/\Delta\), every score contrast, and CACE bounds. When \(\Gamma\ne0\) but \(N=0\), CACE is zero even though the distributional contrast can remain nonidentified.
